<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose  
   - UJCMS is a Java-based, full-stack, enterprise CMS that supports both traditional server-rendered sites (Freemarker templates) and a headless CMS mode (REST API + SPA).  
   - Backend: a monolithic Spring Boot application (Spring Security, MyBatis, Liquibase, Quartz/Flowable, Lucene).  
   - Frontend:  
     • Public site: Freemarker templates under `src/main/webapp/templates`  
     • Admin site (“cp”): Vue3/ElementPlus SPA with assets in `src/main/webapp/cp`, built by Vite/Gulp.

2. High-Level Components  
   - Clients  
     • Public Browser → Freemarker-rendered pages  
     • Admin Browser → Vue3 SPA (calls backend REST)  
   - Spring Boot Application (single deployable jar/war)  
     • Web Layer  
       – Public MVC Controllers (Freemarker)  
       – REST Controllers (API under `/api`, backend API under `/cp/api`)  
     • Service Layer (business logic)  
     • Data Access Layer (MyBatis mappers + domain objects)  
     • Core Modules  
       – SecurityConfig, JwtAuthService  
       – CacheConfig (Spring Cache)  
       – LuceneConfig (embedded full-text search)  
       – ScheduleConfig (Quartz or Spring Scheduler)  
       – MyBatisConfig, SwaggerConfig  
       – AOP (OperationLogAspect)  
     • Extension Module (`com.ujcms.cms.ext`): plugin-style subsystems (collector, survey, message board, import, visit stat, vote, etc.)  
     • Common Libraries (`com.ujcms.commons`): shared utilities (captcha, db helpers, file handlers, freemarker tags, security, SMS, web helper classes)  
   - Persistence  
     • MySQL 8.0 (with Liquibase changelogs under `src/main/resources/db/changelog`)  
     • Freemarker template files and static uploads on filesystem (`/uploads`)  
     • Lucene index files (`WEB-INF/lucene`)  
   - External Services  
     • OAuth providers (Weixin, QQ, Weibo)  
     • SMTP/SMS gateways (Aliyun/Tencent utilities)  
     • Optional Redis or other cache backends if configured  

3. Relationships & Data Flows  
   - Browser → HTTP(S) → Spring Boot Web Layer  
   - Web Layer → Service Layer → Data Access Layer → MySQL  
   - Service Layer ↔ Spring Cache (in-memory or Redis)  
   - Service Layer ↔ Lucene Engine (index + search)  
   - Startup → Liquibase applies DB migrations automatically  
   - Admin SPA → REST API Controllers → Service → DB/Cache  

4. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   - Layered MVC (Controller → Service → Mapper/DAO)  
   - Plugin/Extension architecture (`core` vs `ext` packages)  
   - Headless CMS support: decoupled API layer for modern SPAs  
   - Template-plus-tags for server-rendered mode vs API-first for SPAs  
   - Use of AOP for cross-cutting concerns (logging, security)  
   - Embedded full-text search with Lucene  

5. Diagram Tailoring for UJCMS  
   - Draw two client boxes: “Public Site” (Freemarker) and “Admin SPA” (Vue3)  
   - Show one Spring Boot box subdivided into:  
     • Web Layer (MVC + REST + Backend API)  
     • Core Services (Security, Scheduling, Caching, Lucene, Swagger)  
     • Service Layer & Domain  
     • Data Layer (MyBatis mappers)  
     • Extension Module  
     • Commons Module  
   - Show MySQL box with Liquibase arrow on startup  
   - Show File Store: `/uploads`, `/templates` directory and Lucene index directory  

6. Diagramming Guidelines  
   - Use distinct shapes/colors:  
     • Blue for UI/Clients  
     • Green for application modules  
     • Orange for persistence  
     • Red for external services  
   - Label every component clearly  
   - Use directional arrows to indicate request/response and data flow  
   - Group related packages/modules into composite boxes  
   - Annotate key frameworks (Spring Boot, MyBatis, Freemarker, Vue3/ElementPlus, Lucene)  

7. Essential Elements to Include  
   - Clients: Public Browser, Admin Browser (SPA)  
   - HTTP Layer: MVC Controllers, API Controllers  
   - Business Layer: Services, AOP aspects  
   - Data Layer: MyBatis mappers → MySQL (with Liquibase)  
   - Embedded Search: Lucene index store  
   - File Storage: templates & uploads directories  
   - Extensions: plugin modules under `com.ujcms.cms.ext`  
   - Commons: shared utilities  
   - External: OAuth, SMS/Email services  

By following the above breakdown, you’ll capture UJCMS’s full architecture—showing both server-rendered and headless flows, the layered monolith structure, extension points, and all persistence/search dependencies—ensuring an accurate, detailed system design diagram.  
</explanation>
